question.text: Two charges of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mi>Q</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>Q</mi></math> are situated at the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> respectively. The electric flux through a sphere of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi></math> having centre at origin is:

solution.text:
As can be seen from the figure above, only the 5Q charge is inside the spherical region.

The formula to calculate the flux through the surface is given by

ϕ=qencε0   ...1

From equation (1), the flux through the given surface can be calculated as follows:

ϕ=5Qε0
